newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn may sell some Telekom shares this year.
newsitem.headline: Bonn may sell some Telekom shares this year.

text.p: The German government is considering selling some of its stake in telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom this year, sources in the ruling coalition said on Tuesday.

The sources were confirming the tenor of a report in the business daily Handelsblatt which said Finance Minister Theo Waigel wanted to sell some of the government's holding this year to ease his budget problems.
Telekom went public in Germany's biggest ever share listing six months ago as part of a privatisation plan.
But the government had not planned to sell off any of its stake of just under 75 percent in the former national telecommunications firm before the year 2000.
Bonn now holds around two billion Telekom shares, which at current market prices are worth some 80 billion marks.
Handelsblatt said in an advance release from Wednesday's edition that Bonn had not yet decided how big a stake it wanted to sell this year, and that this would depend on its budget requirements.

Estimates of 1997 tax revenue due to be published on Thursday are likely to show a shortfall of around 20 billion marks, experts say, almost certainly forcing Waigel into a new round of drastic spending cuts.

The parliamentary factions of the parties in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition were due to discuss a range of options on Thursday evening including selling Telekom shares, cutting Federal Labour Office expenditure and imposing a spending freeze, Handelsblatt said.
